findings.reason: the plan's §6 done-when asks for four captures "with their computed geometry", and each capture's fixture re-lists a subset of the canonical stylesheets by hand, so a stylesheet added to the SPA renders in the browser and not in the capture; the plan should derive stylesheet paths from `docs/index.html` (a `authored_stylesheet_paths()` sibling to `authored_ui_module_paths`) or state why it cannot.
findings.text: `_SPA_STYLESHEETS` re-declares the authored stylesheet set whose owner is the canonical SPA index `docs/index.html` (its 12 `<link>` elements, lines 8-19) and has already drifted from it: the harness list omits `ui/home.css`, which `docs/index.html:17` loads; the harness already derives its *script* order from the index via `authored_ui_module_paths` (tests/spa_browser_harness.py:65-79) but not its stylesheet order, so the one list it copies is the one that can drift; the same hand-listed subsets are re-declared at tests/test_spa_crew_geometry.py:107-114 and tests/test_spa_sprints_geometry.py:313-320

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `file_spa` / `write_file_spa_document` (tests/spa_browser_harness.py:557-638) hide runtime-asset loading, JSX compilation through the production compiler, stylesheet and composed-state inlining, and temp-dir lifecycle behind one context manager yielding the existing `ServedSpa` probe interface; the interface is smaller than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the canonical stylesheet set is owned by `docs/index.html` and the shared harness re-declares a hand-maintained subset that has already drifted, a defect that recurs in the geometry fixtures.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; every name this plan adds (`write_file_spa_document`, `file_spa`, the `BrowserProbeError` classifications) lives under `tests/`, and the counted families are read from the `reckon/` package tree only (`reckon/interface_counts.py:1-16`), so no family is added and no retirement or merge is owed in text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §5 enumerates the probe classifier and the skip boundary already in the tree and §6 names the shared harness, choosing to add a second delivery path inside it ("a second delivery path in the harness rather than a second harness") rather than a second harness; the inlined-document writer further reuses `reckon.serve.client_runtime_assets` and `compile_*` rather than re-carrying its own runtimes.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §6 states why the existing harness cannot be used as it stands (it serves over `http://127.0.0.1`, the one scheme the host browser cannot reach), so the new path is a justified second delivery mechanism rather than a forwarding layer over machinery that could simply have been extended.
